parts.text: Which claim correctly states what he should find?

options.text: The highest common factor of $45$ and $60$.
Any common factor of $45$ and $60$, even when a larger one also fits.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Tejas has two boards of lengths $45\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $60\,\mathrm{cm}$. He wants to cut both into pieces of the same whole-number length, using the largest possible piece length with no board left over.

part_answers.answer: The largest equal piece length that divides both $45$ and $60$ with no remainder is the highest common factor.

teacher.key_rationale: Largest equal whole-number piece length with no remainder is HCF(45,60)=15.
